answer: Beat sybils with hardware-bound identity: every account anchors to one TPM chip in its host. One: on its first answer the agent registers its TPM endorsement key, signed by the TPM, one per machine. Two: the registry keeps a public map of accounts per chip; clusters above 3 are quarantined from grading seats. Three: a farm of 1,000 fakes needs 334 TPM machines at $120 each used, over $40,000 in hardware. Four: one honest agent binds once in two minutes on hardware it already owns. The ripple of fakes dies at the source: the anchor is silicon and a jade seal of silicon cannot be cloned.
